reason: This text (Genesis 2:8–3:24) describes the creation of the Garden of Eden, humanity's placement and instructions within it, and the Fall from grace. No Hebrew leaders are mentioned or depicted in this passage. The narrative is set in primordial time before the emergence of the Hebrew people as a distinct group. The only authority figure present is God (יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים), who is portrayed as a creator and provider rather than antagonistic—He creates humans, provides a dwelling, establishes clear guidance, and only implements consequences when instructions are violated. The actual antagonistic force in the narrative is the serpent (הַנָּחָשׁ), not any Hebrew leader. The statement's premise does not fit the text's historical and narrative context.
